title: docs(qa): platform-checklist README and runs/README restate the reproduction obligation without the access-control carve-out
body:
Follow-up finding from the work on #9471 (PR #9506), filed unassigned for triage. It sits
outside that card's declared file surface (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/RUNNER.md` only),
so it was deliberately left untouched there rather than smuggled into that PR.

## What #9471 established

RUNNER.md rule 2 now carries an authentication/authorization carve-out: such a `fail` is a
**completed verdict** when it records the item id, the clause, and `detail withheld pending
maintainer`, with the reproduction held in the runner session and never published anywhere
on GitHub. Three restatements of the obligation inside RUNNER.md were pointed at that
carve-out in the same PR.

## What is still unconditional

Two sibling documents restate the same obligation with no exception:

- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/README.md:282` — "every run files one `qa-run` GitHub issue
  as its record (text only: the verdict table + a reproduction rule per failure, never
  screenshots; `runs/` is git-ignored)"
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/runs/README.md:16` — "**every `fail` carries a reproduction
  rule** in that same issue — ordered steps / API calls (method · path · body) / the
  ref-targeted selector path + expected-vs-actual"

This is the same defect shape #9471 describes: a reader who lands on either document alone
gets the unconditional rule and no hint that a carve-out exists. `runs/README.md` is the
more load-bearing of the two — it is what a runner reads while actually writing the record.

## Suggested shape

A pointer to RUNNER.md rule 2's carve-out in each, **not** a second copy of the policy.
RUNNER.md rule 2 stays the single source; the #9471 PR used pointers for its three in-file
restatements for exactly this reason, and four copies of one disclosure policy is the drift
both cards exist to prevent.

Blocked-by: #9471 — the carve-out these pointers would reference lands with that card's PR.

## Verification bound

Found by grepping `docs/qa/platform-checklist/` for the phrasing while in RUNNER.md.
Documents outside that directory were not swept, so this is not a claim that these two are
the only remaining instances.
